cuts.english: lose stamina, get out of shape
cuts.trap: Stamina 'falls' (saikin tairyoku ochita). English 'lose' pushes learners toward nakusu.
cuts.reason: 'Saikin tairyoku ochita' is a very common adult complaint (judged 4/5), and it pairs with tairyoku ga aru (now added). It only just missed.

cuts.trap: Shots take utsu ('hit'), and the same form covers getting one: wakuchin utta? = did you get your jab?
cuts.reason: Only for vaccinations.

cuts.trap: A bad back is koshi (lower back), not senaka, and the injury verb is itameru, not itaku suru.
cuts.reason: Hurting your back comes up now and then; koshi ga itai (now added) is the everyday complaint.

cuts.trap: English says 'quiet', but shizuka describes places. A person who says little is kuchikazu ga sukunai.
cuts.reason: Means 'quiet, doesn't say much' about a person. It is real but uncommon (4 hits).

cuts.trap: Not nekutai o kiru: a tie is 'tightened' with shimeru, which sounds like shimeru 'close'. Wearing one is just nekutai shiteru.
cuts.reason: nekutai o suru (now on the list) is how people say they're wearing a tie; shimeru is only the act of tying it.

cuts.trap: Not densha ga yameru: yameru is quitting. A train stopping (at a station, or halted) is tomaru.
cuts.reason: In Japan, trains stopping after an accident or a typhoon is a constant excuse (densha tomatteru). Films just don't show it, hence only 3 hits.

cuts.trap: Checking the seasoning is aji o miru ('look at the taste') or ajimi suru; ajiwau means savour.
cuts.reason: Only used for tasting while you cook, and many people say ajimi suru.

cuts.trap: Not netsu o toru: you 'measure' a fever, netsu o hakaru (netsu hakatta?).
cuts.reason: 'Netsu hakatta?' is asked whenever anyone feels ill, and Japanese homes, schools and workplaces check temperatures daily; the film count (3) undersells it. It only just missed.

cuts.trap: Not ashi ga neru or nemuru: a numb, tingling foot is shibireru.
cuts.reason: Mostly heard after sitting seiza (judged 3/5).

cuts.english: the AC is working (cooling or heating properly)
cuts.trap: Not ugoku: for an AC that is running but not cooling, Japanese says it doesn't kiku (take effect), as in kusuri ga kiku. Usually eakon kiitenai.
cuts.reason: Natives rate it 3/5. It's mainly said when the AC isn't keeping up (eakon kiitenai).

cuts.english: be online, be posted on the internet
cuts.trap: Not netto ni aru: being posted or listed is noru (載る), the same sound as getting on a train. Usually netto ni notteru.
cuts.reason: Netto ni notteru ('it's online') is real but much rarer than the kept internet set (3).

cuts.trap: English 'rest up / recover' has no noun. Japanese 'takes off' the tiredness: onsen de tsukare o toru, yukkuri yasunde tsukare totte ne.
cuts.reason: The 'do it' side of tsukare ga toreru (now added), and said less often than that one.

cuts.trap: Not paama o suru or morau: a perm takes kakeru, like an iron (airon o kakeru). At the salon it is paama o kakete morau.
cuts.reason: Means 'get a perm' and only comes up at the hair salon (judged 2).

cuts.english: the alcohol kicks in; start to feel drunk
cuts.trap: English 'it's hitting me' has no verb a learner could map. Feeling the drink kick in is yoi ga mawaru, also osake ga mawaru.
cuts.reason: Only 3 hits and judged 3/5. A nice drinking phrase, but not a top one.

cuts.trap: Heating is often switched on with ireru (danbou irete). Tsukeru also works, as with eakon o tsukeru.
cuts.reason: Danbou tsukeru works just as well, the same tsukeru as denki o tsukeru (only 3 hits for the ireru form).

cuts.trap: The means of payment takes de: kaado de, genkin de (in cash, 14 hits).
cuts.reason: Paying by card is covered by kaado o tsukau, now added, which people say far more (79 vs 3).

cuts.trap: 'Improve' is agaru (go up). Dropping grades are sagaru / ochiru.
cuts.reason: Rare (3). Seiseki ga ii, being added, is the common grades set.

cuts.trap: Backchannelling has its own noun and verb in Japanese, aizuchi o utsu. English has no set phrase for it.
cuts.reason: People do it constantly but rarely name it (2 hits).

cuts.trap: Cross-legged sitting is done with kaku, the same verb as ibiki o kaku and ase o kaku.
cuts.reason: Sitting cross-legged comes up only now and then (3 hits, judged 3/5).

cuts.trap: Not haka o houmon suru. Visiting a grave is ohakamairi, done at Obon, during higan and at New Year.
cuts.reason: Obon, higan and New Year only (13 hits for the noun).

cuts.trap: Not kisetsu, which is a season of the year. Flavouring food is aji o tsukeru, or the noun ajitsuke.
cuts.reason: Cooking-only. Seasoning a dish comes up in the kitchen or in recipes (3 hits).

cuts.english: air the futon in the sun

cuts.trap: Fog 'hangs' (kakaru): kiri ga kakatte mienai. Kiri ga deru is also said.

cuts.trap: Not kuchi o arau. Rinsing is yusugu; dentists say kuchi o yusuide kudasai.

cuts.ja: アクセサリーを付ける

cuts.trap: No English verb leads here: bed hair 'sticks on' (neguse ga tsuku), as in neguse tsuiteru yo.

cuts.trap: Not sentakuki o hashiraseru or ugokasu: you 'spin' (mawasu) the washer.
